strict_helper_replay.scope: Replay current unchanged RSS helper on15second downsampled periodic Linux HTTP diagnostic samples, not actual UI or a new live test

method_notes: Random session token generated only inside isolated container, never printed. Repository mounted read-only, data temporary, models/enrichment disabled, no user containers altered.

All requests use actual secure_entry/production service/router/storage paths over authenticated localhost HTTP. Seven-route API cycles are a targeted backend diagnostic, not eight-view browser navigation equivalence.
Each run seeds1000synthetic records, uses four writer/six reader client workers, three initial query cycles followed by150additional cycles; server thread count includes the diagnostic monitor.

Traced run starts tracemalloc5frames before imports. Snapshot metadata heavily inflates RSS and GC object counts; absolute traced RSS is not production capacity evidence. Net retained allocation differences are compared only within that run.

GC runs at fixed diagnostic checkpoints, after requests finish; periodic samples may occur during requests. malloc_trim(0) runs once after workload, only in isolated diagnostic wrapper. Neither GC nor trimming was added to production Core.
Plain-run tracing fields are omitted because tracing was disabled; private common-collector zero placeholders do not mean zero heap.
The paced case runs153cycles at2second minimum cadence (~309.58s with checkpoint overhead). Its helper result is an offline replay on15second downsampled periodic metrics, not an actual UI assertion.
Released RSS after malloc_trim demonstrates allocator-held free pages in these reproductions; it does not prove every CI RSS increment has that cause or exclude all untracked native/slow/late leaks.
No memory threshold or warmup deadline changes were made after the failed de3 run. Current strict120second warmup and full requested120second measurement passed actual afaa CI.
The isolated Python3.12.15 diagnostic is historical evidence, not a recommendation for the final packaged interpreter; later release-runtime security changes require their own CI proof.
